Students considering this major are strongly urged to review the University Catalog for further information about this major, the concentrations, emphases and other upper division course options. Many of the areas below are primarily composed of upper division coursework not reflected here on ASSIST, only lower division courses are published.Humboldt’s program is unique among the child development programs in that:core courses (which all students take) give cohesive and comprehensive attention to children’s development and socialization;an on-campus practicum is required;additional practicums with children or families are available in the emphasis areas;coursework beyond the core is based on the student’s own identified special interests.In core courses students learn basic principles and theories of child development as well as practices that support children and families. Students select one of the following three concentrations: Child and Family Services, Teaching or Specialized Studies. Within the first two concentrations, students also select an emphasis. The Specialized Studies concentration is individually designed between student and advisor.Important note for transfer students: Students may not use the same transferable course for both CD 253 and CD 255. Please select another course to meet the remaining courses required.

Students considering this major are strongly urged to review the University Catalog for further information about this major, the concentrations, emphases and other upper division course options. Many of the areas below are primarily composed of upper division coursework not reflected here on ASSIST, only lower division courses are published.Humboldt’s program is unique among the child development programs in that:core courses (which all students take) give cohesive and comprehensive attention to children’s development and socialization;an on-campus practicum is required;additional practicums with children or families are available in the emphasis areas;coursework beyond the core is based on the student’s own identified special interests.In core courses students learn basic principles and theories of child development as well as practices that support children and families. Students select one of the following three concentrations: Child and Family Services, Teaching or Specialized Studies. Within the first two concentrations, students also select an emphasis. The Specialized Studies concentration is individually designed between student and advisor.Important note for transfer students: Students may not use the same transferable course for both CD 253 and CD 255. Please select another course to meet the remaining courses required.

Art is a cohort-based program for students in their junior and senior years.The degree is a 120-unit program requiring 70 units of courses in studio and art history, giving students the opportunity to develop a high level of expertise within their chosen concentration(s). The BFA is the degree of choice for students interested in pursuing graduate studies or other professional opportunities. The lower division coursework is designed to give students a solid technical foundation in studio art. Students at the upper division level focus their study in consultation with an advisor on approved elective courses in painting, drawing and illustration, jewelry and small metals, photography, ceramics, printmaking, sculpture, and digital media/graphic design. The upper division component is tailored to each student’s individual studio emphasis. Through problem-solving assignments and accompanying instruction, students learn processes and strategies for creating works of art in various media. By concentrating on a particular studio area in depth, students can prepare a portfolio for further professional opportunities or for postgraduate study. Note - students who wish to pursue a minor or second major in another field, should consult with an advisor and may find that the B.A. degree in Art with a concentration in Studio Art a more attractive option with greater flexibility.Admission Requirements & Procedures:Admission to the program is competitive. To be considered, an applicant must have completed the lower division core courses in the art major (15 units) and two lower division studio elective courses in the art studio concentration with a minimum GPA of 3.00 (B average). In addition, applicants are required to electronically submit images of their work, two academic references, a short personal statement and an unofficial transcript. Transfer students interested in the B.F.A. program may apply to the program following the above guidelines. Students must meet university admission requirements as well as the BFA admission requirements.For university transfer requirements, see the “Admission Information” section of the catalog.Please refer There are no lower division prerequisites for the courses in the major. The courses are 100% online. To learn more, contact the Department at https://extended.humboldt.edu/leadership-studies Preparation: This is a degree completion program designed for upper division transfer students and working adults who want to customize their learning experience to align with their current professional goals. An associates degree is NOT required to be admitted to the Leadership Studies major, although many applicants do have an associates degree prior to applying. To be admitted, applicants must complete -- before the application term -- at least 60 and up to 70 units of lower division coursework with at least a 2.0 cumulative grade point average based on their transferable work. Within those 60-70 units, they must complete at least 30 units of general education (GE) coursework with grades of C- or higher. As part of those 30 GE units, they must complete, with C- or better, all four of these subject areas: Written Communication (English Composition); Oral Communication (Public Speaking); Critical Thinking; and Mathematics/Quantitative Reasoning. For more information on how to apply: https://extended.humboldt.edu/leadership-studies/apply\r\nFee Structure: Students pay per course instead of paying full time or part time tuition rates. Because the Leadership Studies Program is delivered by the College Extended Education & Global Engagement, students are not subject to HSU state fees. Self-support programs do not receive tax dollars from the State. Therefore, please be aware that State University Grants, Cal Grants and fee waivers cannot be applied to pay for this program. ","groupId":"2fb07645-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":0,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"About the BFA Program:The Bachelor of Fine Arts (B.F.A.) in Fine Art is a cohort-based program for students in their junior and senior years.The degree is a 120-unit program requiring 70 units of courses in studio and art history, giving students the opportunity to develop a high level of expertise within their chosen concentration(s). The BFA is the degree of choice for students interested in pursuing graduate studies or other professional opportunities. The lower division coursework is designed to give students a solid technical foundation in studio art. Students at the upper division level focus their study in consultation with an advisor on approved elective courses in painting, drawing and illustration, jewelry and small metals, photography, ceramics, printmaking, sculpture, and digital media/graphic design. The upper division component is tailored to each student’s individual studio emphasis. Through problem-solving assignments and accompanying instruction, students learn processes and strategies for creating works of art in various media. By concentrating on a particular studio area in depth, students can prepare a portfolio for further professional opportunities or for postgraduate study. Note - students who wish to pursue a minor or second major in another field, should consult with an advisor and may find that the B.A. degree in Art with a concentration in Studio Art a more attractive option with greater flexibility.Admission Requirements & Procedures:Admission to the program is competitive. To be considered, an applicant must have completed the lower division core courses in the art major (15 units) and two lower division studio elective courses in the art studio concentration with a minimum GPA of 3.00 (B average). In addition, applicants are required to electronically submit images of their work, two academic references, a short personal statement and an unofficial transcript. Transfer students interested in the B.F.A. program may apply to the program following the above guidelines. Students must meet university admission requirements as well as the BFA admission requirements.For university transfer requirements, see the “Admission Information” section of the catalog.Please refer is an RN to BSN program.The Nursing RN to BSN program at Cal Poly Humboldt is designed for students who have earned an associate degree in nursing, hold a Registered Nursing (RN) license, and want to advance their skills in leadership, care management and health promotion. The program’s curriculum is designed specifically for our area, focusing on physical and psychosocial health needs and problems within the region’s rural and tribal communities. The program accommodates working nurses with a flexible blend of online and in-person courses.Program Admission RequirementsTo be eligible for admission to the program, candidates must:be a graduate of a nationally recognized, regionally accredited associate degree program in nursinghave a current, clear, and active California Registered Nursing (RN) licensehave a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.75 from all transfer institutionshave completed the eight CSU systemwide nursing program prerequisites as outlined under Prerequisites to the Major belowmaintain current California R.N. licensure while enrolled in nursing coursesit is the student's responsibility to notify the program director immediately, in writing, of any changes in licensure statusLearn more at nursing.humboldt.edu/","groupId":"62a97645-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":4,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"
